This is really how I feel a lot of the time. As Lag-Wagon said you need to love yourself first. If you don't love yourself you won't even be able to accept that someone else does love you. I'm in a rough patch of my relationship at the minute and I don't feel particularly loved. The brief times that I get some love don't make up for the lengthy periods I'm left to my own self loathing that has managed to destroy any love I ever felt.

Like others have said you need to learn how to love yourself, if you do not love yourself then imagine your heart like a mug with a hole drilled through the bottom. You can hold onto it and initially it feels nice but eventually it will dribble out and you will be left at square one. It is very important to learn how to patch up this whole and to love yourself again.

An important thing and probably the first thing you should consider doing is to learn how to forgive, especially learn how to forgive yourself. This is difficult to manage at first, especially if you are stuck in an endless loop of self-deprecation, loathing and low self-esteem. It may feel foreign at first to because you have never experienced it before. The important thing is to catch yourself and monitor your own behaviour and if you start having negative thoughts stop yourself in your tracks and replace it with a light compliment. The point of this exercise is to gradually change your entire perspective of yourself. Keep this up and be consistent otherwise it will probably fail. Forgiveness is the first step to healing, if you haven't forgiven whatever it is that may be keeping you anchored to the past then you will never be able to move forward.

Forgive yourself, for you are only human and it is human nature to fall down occasionally. It is human nature to get stuck in ruts, it is human nature to dwell. That being said, it is human nature to brush off the dust and climb back to your feet. It is human nature to look at the past and learn to smile, instead of seeing it as something that detracts from you, think of it as something that gives you character and makes you what you are today, stronger and more resilient.

Don't take this the wrong way but the self-deprecation loop is selfish, you become consumed with yourself and become the single most important thing in your life, without realising it you only care about your own wellbeing and forget about those around you, even if they're showering you with care and love you brush it off like it is nothing, you become like a blackhole that just sucks in any light and positivity and it is never seen again. What I mean by that is that you become familiar with self-loathing and you perhaps unknowingly spell out your own fate because you are used to it happening, it is easier to feel this way than it is to actually face everything and rise above it. Let me tell you though that is exponentially better to overcome, you are granted a new lease on life, you begin to feel whole, like a deserving human being. Instead of questioning everything and wondering whether you're deserving you just enjoy it.

I think the next thing to help with the healing is to take up an interest, something that keeps you motivated and lifts your spirits. Something that gets you out of bed in the morning. Doesn't matter what it is as long as you have a passion for it and enjoy doing it. It can be reinvigorating to your soul if it is something you are strongly passionate for.

So just to distill a little basically what needs to be done is:

⚈ Forgiveness: You need to forgive yourself or whatever external factor may be anchoring you. You also, if applicable, need to stop shifting the blame to someone or something else. It is YOUR responsibility to heal yourself and you have to take the Driver's seat and steer yourself back to recovery and to forgiveness, shifting blame only adds to the cycle of self-deprecation.

⚈ Shifting perspective: Catch yourself whenever you have negative thoughts or are putting yourself down and immediately replace it with a light compliment, even if it doesn't feel genuine, just keep doing it. Like the old adage, fake it until you make it.

"Oh I'm so pathe- No! No. I am deserving of forgiveness."

⚈ Pursue an interest: Completely optional but in my opinion just helps you much more along the way, you gain a bit of self-confidence too as you begin to realise that you are actually capable of more than you might currently give yourself credit for. Painting, drawing, dancing, knitting, crafts whatever. Something that is proactive and gets you creating.

In closing, yes you have to love yourself in order to be loved and to love back. I wish you the best of luck in healing and before I forget, the most important ingredient on the road to recovery is that you need to WANT to change for the better, otherwise you can forget it. Couple that with faith that you will succeed in getting better and you've already taken a big step in the right direction. 😊
